main_text.head: UNIVERSAE Philosophiae diuisio.
main_text.p: ONTEM uniuersæ philosophiæ ac principium metemhomi-nis esse, rectè Aristote-les,in primo Analytic.libro,ostendere videtur: quādoquidem homo non solùm rationis particeps est,sed etiam rerum agendarum consiliis : ex quibus vtraque humanæ mentis functio oriri videtur. Vna namque rerum æternarum meditatio est, altera in actio-ne & consilio versatur. Quare ipse Philosophus,in primo diuinæ scientiæ libro , duplex philosophiæ genus ponit , vnum quod θεωρητικὸν est, & alterū πρακτικὸν. Hu-ius

page.notes: The opening word is a decorative woodcut initial "E" joined to "ONTEM", so the first word is printed as "EONTEM"; I have given it as "ONTEM" after the initial, with the initial letter read as E ("Ontem" → "Ontem" in small capitals). The Greek words are printed in Greek letters as shown: θεωρητικὸν and πρακτικὸν are transcribed from the scan, with the first Greek word partly damaged and possibly misread [?]. The word "metemhomi-nis" appears with a black mark (ink blot) over "e" in "metem" and the letters "hom" are partly obscured; the reading "metemhomi-nis" is as printed. "uniuersæ" has an ink blot over "v" that may obscure the letter. The last line "ius" is an incomplete word at the end of the visible text, continuing on the next page. The word "consiliis :" has a space before the colon as printed. No running head, page number, catchword or signature is visible on this page.
